description: We’re 3 CS students tackling “Martian Map”: an interactive Mars map that turns NASA data into safe, clear Marswalk routes. Shraddha: Python backend, data, AI/LLM & map front-end (Leaflet/MapLibre). Vivek Kumar: deployment & testing. Rashmi Gupta: UI/UX design. We’re organized, clear on roles, and aiming for a polished live demo within 48 hours. Our team is complete, but we’d love to connect with other participants and share ideas!
summary:
Cairn is an interactive Mars walking map for astronaut mission planning, built around Jezero Crater. A crew picks a destination, and Cairn compares three routes: safest, shortest, and science-focused. Each route shows distance, walking time, slope, science value, and safety rating, along with science stops, emergency stops, and a Perseverance photo preview. As the crew moves along a route, Cairn calculates the resources needed to return, identifies the turn-back point, and shows GREEN, AMBER, or RED safety alerts, followed by a mission briefing with an automatic fallback if AI is unavailable.

It addresses the challenge by layering Mars Trek imagery with terrain, hazard, and route information for one specific site, and by putting crew safety first. Elevation, slope, and hazard layers are currently synthetic demo data, clearly labelled as assumptions.

Most Mars maps show where the science is. Cairn also shows whether astronauts can safely return, so crews can explore ambitiously and know when to turn back.
details:
What it does and how it works

Cairn is an interactive Mars walking map built around Jezero Crater. The crew picks a destination, and the FastAPI backend builds a cost grid from slope and hazard data, then finds three routes: safest, shortest, and science-focused. The map shows distance, walking time, slope, science value, and safety rating for each, plus science stops, emergency stops, and a Perseverance photo preview. As the crew moves along a chosen route with the progress slider, Cairn calculates the return time, the resources needed to get back, the reserve, and the turn-back point. It then shows GREEN, AMBER, or RED alerts and points to the nearest emergency stop. A mission briefing summarises the situation in plain language, with an automatic template fallback if the AI is unavailable.

Benefits

  • Shows whether the crew can get home, not just where the science is
  • Lets planners compare routes by safety, time, and science value
  • Gives a clear, readable alert state during a walk
  • Keeps assumptions visible and adjustable

Intended impact

Cairn aims to make return-journey safety a standard part of Mars surface planning. It would help mission planners and crews decide where to explore and when to turn back, and the same approach could extend to other sites and the Moon.

Tools and technologies

  • Front-end: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet (React-Leaflet)
  • Back-end: Python, FastAPI, NumPy
  • Data: NASA JPL Mars Trek imagery and a Perseverance rover image, with synthetic terrain for the demo
  • AI: an optional LLM endpoint for the briefing, with a template fallback
  • Other: GitHub for version control
  • Hardware: standard laptops only, no special hardware

Creativity

Cairn treats the return journey as a primary mission constraint, a “trail rating” system for Mars. The name comes from the stack of stones that marks a trail. The GREEN, AMBER, and RED alerts and the turn-back calculation turn terrain and resource data into a single decision a crew can act on quickly.

Factors our team considered

  • Crew safety first: the return journey drives the design
  • Honesty about data: synthetic elevation, slope, and hazard layers are clearly labelled as assumptions, and only real imagery is presented as real
  • Data limits: the Perseverance photo is not georegistered, and the CRISM mineral product we checked falls outside Jezero, so it is not yet integrated
  • Scope: one site, done properly, rather than the whole planet
  • Reliability: the briefing works even when AI is unavailable
  • Readability: a simple interface a crew can read in seconds
